topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

outline.topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rate
sections.content: Briefly visualize the derivative as the 'speedometer' of a function. Introduce the concept of a function machine: an input x goes in, f(x) comes out. Emphasize that we are now looking at functions within functions (nested) and products of functions.
sections.example: An animation of a car's speed (derivative) changing as it travels along a winding road.

sections.title: The Product Rule: The Collaborative Duo
sections.content: When two functions, u(x) and v(x), are multiplied, the derivative isn't just the product of their derivatives. Use an area-model animation: a rectangle with sides u(x) and v(x) expanding. The change in area is the sum of two strips: u(x)dv + v(x)du.
sections.example: A cat running (function u) while carrying a toy that is growing in size (function v). The total 'growth' of the scene depends on both variables changing simultaneously.

sections.title: The Chain Rule: The Nested Gears
sections.content: Visualize the chain rule as a system of gears. If Gear A turns Gear B, and Gear B turns Gear C, the speed of C is the product of the gear ratios. Formula: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x).
sections.example: A mechanical robot arm: the shoulder rotation (outer function) affects the wrist position (inner function). To find the velocity of the hand, you multiply the angular change of the shoulder by the reach change of the arm.

sections.title: Interactive Synthesis: Putting it Together
sections.content: Demonstrate a complex function that requires both rules. Explain the 'Out-to-In' strategy: peel the layers like an onion (Chain Rule) and look for internal products (Product Rule).
sections.example: A rocket launch: the fuel consumption (inner) is multiplied by the altitude gain (outer). We calculate the total 'jerk' (acceleration change) using the product rule while applying the chain rule to the time-dependent fuel pressure.

sections.title: Conclusion & Summary
sections.content: Recap: Product Rule = 'uv' + 'vu' (derivative alternation). Chain Rule = 'Outside derivative' * 'Inside derivative'. Quick visual summary of the gear-and-rectangle animation.
sections.example: A final visual cheat-sheet showing the two formulas appearing on a screen like HUD data for the robot from Section 3.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rate
lecture_lines: Derivatives measure instantaneous change as a rate.
Think of functions as input-output machines.
Complex functions nest or multiply smaller ones.
animations: Create an animation showing a function as a machine [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/machine.svg] taking 'x' as input to produce 'f(x)' output, color: #FFFFFF.
Demonstrate the concept of instantaneous change as a tangent line slope on a curve, color: #00FF00.
Animate two functions nesting or multiplying to show their interaction, color: #FF00FF.

storyboard.title: The Product Rule: The Collaborative Duo
lecture_lines: Multiplying functions creates a growing area.
Area change requires both sides changing.
The Product Rule sums these two effects.
animations: Visualise a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rectangle.svg] with sides u(x) and v(x) growing, color: #FFFF00.
Animate the change in area of the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rectangle.svg] by expanding width and height independently, color: #00FFFF.
Display the formula u'(x)v(x) + u(x)v'(x) with color coding for each term, color: #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: The Chain Rule: The Nested Gears
lecture_lines: Nested functions act like rotating gears.
Turning one gear moves the next one.
Multiply gear ratios for total speed.
animations: Create two connected gears [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gears.svg] representing nested functions f(g(x)), color: #FFA500.
Show the first gear [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gears.svg] turning and causing the second gear to move proportionally, color: #FF4500.
Label the gear ratios as f'(g(x)) and g'(x) and highlight their product, color: #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Interactive Synthesis: Putting it Together
lecture_lines: Analyze complex functions from outside in.
Peel layers with the Chain Rule.
Identify internal products for the Product Rule.
animations: Animate a complex function composed of nested layers, visualized as an [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/onion.svg], color: #00BFFF.
Show the process of 'peeling' away the outer layer of the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/onion.svg] with the Chain Rule, color: #FF1493.
Identify and highlight product sub-structures within the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/onion.svg] to apply the Product Rule, color: #32CD32.

storyboard.title: Conclusion & Summary
lecture_lines: Product Rule: Derivative of u times v.
Chain Rule: Outer derivative times inner derivative.
Master these rules to model change.
animations: Place the formula (uv)' = u'v + uv' in a central box, color: #FFFF00. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Place the formula (f(g))' = f'(g)g' below it in a central box, color: #FF4500.
Show a final summary graphic with both formulas and a checkmark, color: #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
